title: SREV-004 taskbar AppUserModelID process-parameter workaround

appid_api_shape.description: SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID(PCWSTR AppID) returns HRESULT and must be called during initial startup before UI or Jump List manipulation

process_parameters_shape.description: PEB and RTL_USER_PROCESS_PARAMETERS are internal OS structures; public shape exposes only ImagePathName and CommandLine; WindowFlags is not part of the public contract

workaround_owner.description: Taskbar_SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID_hack saves WindowFlags, clears 0x5000 across the real API call, restores only the saved 0x5000 bits

mutation_invariant.description: No permanent ProcessParms->WindowFlags mutation remains after the workaround returns

preservation_invariant.description: WindowFlags bits outside 0x5000 that the real API changes during the call are preserved

runtime_matrix.description: Windows runtime gate: process-level AppUserModelID still works, WindowTitle crash does not return, later process-parameter reads observe the original 0x5000 bits

contracts: SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID assigns an AppUserModelID to the current process and returns HRESULT S_OK on success
SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID must be called during initial startup before UI or Jump List manipulation
RTL_USER_PROCESS_PARAMETERS layout outside ImagePathName/CommandLine is reserved for internal use
WindowFlags is not part of the public process-parameter contract and may change across OS versions
Hack must save WindowFlags before clearing the 0x5000 bits
Hack must clear only 0x5000 while calling the real Shell API
Hack must restore the saved 0x5000 bits after the call without overwriting other WindowFlags changes
Hack must fall back to the direct API call when Proc_GetRtlUserProcessParameters returns NULL
